title: Close a hardback notebook whose cover springs open and fasten it with its elastic band
instruction: Close the notebook and fasten it shut with its elastic band, then let go of it.
context: Pocket notebooks with an elastic closure band are on desks and in bags everywhere; the Moleskine Classic Large hard cover (13 x 21 cm) is sold with "an elastic closure". Closed, the band runs from the back cover over the head, along the front cover near the fore-edge and over the tail back to the back cover, holding the cover shut. Here the cover of a new notebook springs back open (to about 70 degrees) unless held, and the band lies across the first page, where it snaps when the cover is opened with the band on. Shut the cover first and the band is shut inside. So one hand draws the band out past the fore-edge and holds it there while the other shuts the cover and keeps it shut; then the band is stretched up over the fore-edge, high enough that its ends ride over the cover's head and tail corners, and laid across the cover. The hand skill: pinching a 5 mm elastic off a flat page, pulling it out without dragging the 0.3 kg book, and placing it under tension.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. (1) Hardback notebook, Moleskine Classic Large size (21 x 13 x 1.7 cm, about 0.30 kg; red cloth-covered 2.5 mm boards with rounded fore-edge corners, 12 mm ivory page block), loose, lying back cover down at x 12 to 33, y -6.5 to 6.5: head away from the robot, fore-edge toward the robot's right (y -6.5), spine at y 6.5. Its front cover stands open 70 degrees; the new notebook's stiff spine springs it back to 70 degrees whenever it is let go (about 3 N pressed 6 cm from the spine holds it shut). (2) Its black elastic closure band, 5 mm wide, 22.6 cm unstretched, sewn into the back board at the tail and head edges 1 cm in from the fore-edge (x 11.8 and 33.2, y -5.5); it runs up the tail and head and lies stretched across the first page along y -5.5 (about 2 N). Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read every control step from the poses of the notebook, its cover and the band, and the fingers' collision hulls. Shut: the front cover within 3 degrees of the pages (fore-edge within 7 mm of them); it springs open unless something holds it. Band on: the band's middle on the front cover's face, at most 4 mm above it and at least 3 mm in from its fore-edge. Released and still: every finger point 3 cm or more from the notebook, cover and band; the notebook flat on the desk (tilt under 5 degrees); nothing moving more than 2 mm in the last second. 1.0 (success, held 1 s): shut, band on, released and still. 0.3: shut, released and still, but the band's middle not on the cover (caught round the fore-edge). 0 otherwise (cover open, still held, or the notebook tipped). Nothing is latched; sliding the notebook costs nothing. Real trial: a photo after the arms move away, and a ruler for the cover's gap.
reset_notes: Take the band off, open the front cover with the band on so that the band snaps across the first page, let the cover spring back to its rest angle, and lay the notebook back on its marks (tape at two corners). Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz. The notebook is one rigid body with the front cover on a sprung hinge (0.15 N m/rad toward 70 degrees: a new notebook's stiff spine; a real one's rest angle is measured). The band is 16 rigid 2 g links: two sewn-in roots (sprung upright, 0.02 N m/rad) and 14 links on ball joints that stretch (80 N/m for the band, an estimate); it lies within 2 mm of the cover when fastened. Friction 0.3 band, 0.45 book on desk (estimates).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the left gripper pushed the cover nearly shut with the band still on the pages under it, the right gripper hovered by the fore-edge, and the cover sprang back open); demo: 1.0
